JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this Petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the Death of one Jagadish R.S. in a road traffic accident dated 18.01.2023.
2.

The case of the Petitioners' in brief is that:
On 18.01.2023 at about 05.30pm when the deceased Jagadeesh and Kumar were proceeding in a Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-54-Q-8524 carefully observing traffic rules and regulations on NH-75 Hassan - Bangalore Road infront of Milk Dairy Chakenahalli Yediyur Hobli Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District on left side of the Road,
another motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EP-2040 came from opposite wrong side in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life without SCCH-25 observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the deceased's motorcycle.
Due to that impact the deceased Jagadish suffered injuries.

3. It is the further case of the petitioners that, immediately, he was shifted to Yediyur Govt. Hospital wherein first aid treatment was given, due to severe injuries he was referred to Shreyas Hospital at Bangalore wherein he took treatment.
During the course of treatment he died in the hospital and the Srinivasa vs Nanjundegowda on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56326185/
2 dead body was shifted to AIMS Hospital at BG Nagar wherein Postmortem examination was conducted and handed over the dead body to the petitioners.
Thereafter the petitioners performed funeral and obsequies by spending Rs.2,00,000/-.
Due to the sudden and sad demise of Jagadish R.S. in the tragic accident the petitioners are undergoing deep mental shock pain and sufferings.

4. It is the further case of the petitioners that, prior to the date of accident the deceased Jagadish R.S. was hale and SCCH-25 healthy, he was Hotel Employee and earning of Rs.30,000/- per month and contributing entire amount to the maintenance of the family.
Due to sudden demise of the deceased Jagadish, the petitioners have lost their bread earner of the family.
The accident was only due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the said offending vehicle bearing No.KA-13-EP-2040.
The jurisdictional Amrutur police have registered a case and filed charge sheet against the rider of the said vehicle in Cr.No.13/2023 p/u/Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.

The 1 st respondent being the RC owner of the aforesaid motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EP-2040 and 2nd Respondent being the RC owner of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-54-Q-8524 and 3rd respondent being the insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
5. In response to the service of notice, the Respondent Nos.2 & 3 appeared through their respective counsels and filed SCCH-25 separate written statements.
In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear hence, placed ex-parte.

6. The objections of the Respondent No.2:
He has admitted the ownership of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-54-Q-8524 and stated that all the records of the motorcycle are standing in his name.

Further admitted that his vehicle was/is insured with the 3rd respondent i.e.,
Cholamandalam MS General Ins. Co. Ltd.,

Hence the above case is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.

7. The objections of the Respondent No.3:

The policy covers the risk of only Third party, the premium is collected only to cover the risk of third parties and no additional premium is collected to cover the risk of pillion rider who are found to be traveling in the motorcycle.
Further submitted that IO has filed chargesheet against the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA13-EP-2040.

1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased Sri. Jagadish R.?

Tumkur, due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EP-2040 as alleged?

REASONS 12. Issue No.1:
It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the Father, Petitioner No.2 is the Mother and Petitioner No.3 is the younger Brother of the deceased - Jagadish Srinivasa vs Nanjundegowda on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56326185/
4 R.
The Petitioners to prove their relationship have examined the 1 st SCCH-25 Petitioner as PW.1.
PW.1 has specifically spoken about this relationship in his chief-examination.
Apart from that, to prove the relationship, the Petitioners have also produced Notarized copy of Aadhar card of the petitioners and the deceased as per Ex.P.8.
In the Aadhar card of the petitioner No.1, his father's name is mentioned as Manthaiah.

In the Aadhar Card of the petitioner No.2, her husband's name is shown as Srinivasa and in the Aadhar Card of the petitioner No.3, his father's name is shown as Srinivasa who is the petitioner No.1 in this case.
In the same manner in the Aadhar card of the deceased, his father's name is shown as Srinivasa who is the petitioner No.1.
In Ex.P.5/Inquest report, deceased's father is shown as Srinivas.
These documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents.
The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral SCCH-25 and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and the documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 is the Father,
Petitioner No.2 is the Mother and petitioner No.3 is the younger brother of the deceased Jagadish R..
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:

The Petitioners to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle have examined Petitioner No.1 as PW.1 and produced documents as per Exs.P.1 to 7.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.

On the other hand,
the Respondent No.3 has denied the involvement and negligence of the insured vehicle.
Further stated that the charge sheet filed against the rider of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-13-EP- 2040.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.
SCCH-25 14.

The documents produced by the Petitioners such as the FIR in Cr.No.13/2023 of Amruthur Traffic Police with Complaint, spot mahazar and seizure mahazar 2 in Nos., spot sketch, IMV report,
inquest report, PM report and charge sheet as per Exs.P.1 to 7 are all public documents and have initial presumptive value under law.
These documents fully and completely corroborate with the evidence of PW.1.

The investigation officer in crime No.13/2023 of Amruthur Police has conducted the investigation in detail and has filed the charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-EP-2040 holding that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the said vehicle p/u/Sec.279, 337, 338, 304(A) r/w Sec.3, 181, 196, 134(A)(B), 187 of MV Act.
During the cross examination of PW.1, he has stated that the bike was in the name of his friend Kumar who is the rider of the bike.
The deceased was pillion rider.
The accident spot is in between Yediyur and Kunigal.
The offending vehicle came from the opposite direction.

Further admitted that Srinivasa vs Nanjundegowda on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56326185/

sentences.text: However, the Respondent No.1 has not obtained any contrary admission from the mouth of PW.1 to show the negligence of the deceased.

Therefore, there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence of PW.1.
15.
The Inquest report and PM report produced as per Exs.P.6 & 7 clearly show that 'Death is due to Intracranial Haemorrhage as a result of head injury sustained'.

Ex.P.6 - MVA report shows that the vehicle bearing No.KA-13-EP-2040 got damaged to its Crash guard at left side, front mudguard and front number plate damaged and the motorcycle bearing No.KA- 54-Q-8524 got damaged to its front mudguard, front body and front left side body, near foot rest damaged.
In support of their defence the respondent No.3 got examined RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1/copy of insurance policy.
During the cross examination of RW.1 she has admitted that the charge sheet is not filed against its insured vehicle.
The accident is head on SCCH-25 collision.
The policy was valid.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was caused due to the negligence of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EP-2040.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
16.
Issue No. 3:
PW.1 has specifically spoken before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, they have lost the bread earner of their family and his loving son.

He has further deposed that they have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment,
transportation of dead body and the funeral expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation as per the following discussion.
Monthly income 17.
According to the Petitioners, the deceased was Hotel Employee and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
In this regard, the Petitioners have not produced any documents such as Bank statement, payslips etc., nor have they examined SCCH-25 any witness.
The accident occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.16,000/- per month.
Age of the deceased 18.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced the notarized copy of Aadhar Card of the deceased at Ex.P.8.
As per Ex.P.8, the date of birth of the deceased is 22.05.1997 and the accident occurred on 18.01.2023.
Therefore, the deceased was aged about 25 years as on the date of accident.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
Therefore, his age is considered as 25 years.

(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE PROSPECTS:-
As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.

sentences.text: PW.1 in his cross - examination admitted that his another son is sick and at home.
As such it can be considered that petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are considered as the dependents of the deceased.
However if the notional income is applied to the deceased, he would be earning around Rs.16,000/- per month.
19. As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As mentioned above, since the deceased was under below 40 years age slab, 40% future prospects is to be added to his monthly income.
So Rs.6,400/- (Rs.16,000/- X 40% = Rs.6,400/-) should be added to his monthly salary of Rs.16,000/- then it comes to Rs.22,400/- per month.
As per the Sarala Verma case, if the deceased is a bachelor then 1/2 of his income has to be deducted towards his SCCH-25 personal and living expenses, balance comes to Rs.11,200/-.
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.24,19,200/- (Rs.11,200/- X 18 x 12 = Rs.24,19,200/-).

(ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:-
In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130

entities.text: Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.

With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".
20.
This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780. SCCH-25 21.

entities.text: United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780. SCCH-25 21
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 is the Father and the petitioner No.2 are the Mother of the deceased.
The Mother and father have to live remaining part of their life in the absence of their young son.
The loss of a young son full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to the parents.
Therefore, petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,000/- each total Rs.96,000/- under the head of loss of consortium.

(iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES AND LOSS OF ESTATE:-
In so far as the funeral and transportation expenses are concerned, the Petitioners have contended that they have spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
But, there is no document produced in this regard.
The deceased was at Yediyur Govt. Hospital at Yediyur and thereafter shifted to Shreyas Hospital, Bangalore, wherein took under treatment succumbed fatal injuries the deceased was died.
In addition there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.

sentences.text: Therefore, in the interest of justice the Petitioners are awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
If the deceased was alive he would have certainly saved some amount out of his living and personal expenses and created an estate in favour of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of estate.

Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for a total sum of Rs.25,55,200/-.
Liability 22.
The Respondent No.3 has contended that the charge sheet was filed against the respondent No.1 and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the insured motorcycle.

On perusal of the documents on record also it is clear that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EP-2040 and the charge sheet is filed against him.
It is a fact that the said motorcycle was not covered by an insurance as on the date of accident.
Such being SCCH-25 the case, the petitioners have made owner and the insurer of the motorcycle in which the deceased was traveling as a pillion rider as parties to the case.
In the absence of any negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-54-Q- 8524, the owner and the insurer cannot be held liable to pay compensation.
Moreover, the policy did not have own damage coverage to include the pillion rider.
Therefore, the respondent Nos.2 & 3 are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
On the other hand, since the respondent No.1 has not insured his vehicle, the entire liability of paying the compensation is on him.
The Petitioners have claimed an amount of Rs.50,00,000/-, but they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.25,55,200/-.
Therefore the Petition is liable to be allowed.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.4:-

In view of the findings of the above issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:

Moreover, the policy did not have own damage coverage to include the pillion rider.
